data.summary: Investigate further is the recommendation for the Jegadeesh and Titman six-month momentum strategy, which buys the decile of stocks with the highest past six-month returns and holds each monthly cohort for six months. Our long-only test on a 415-name S&P 500 survivor universe over 2015 to 2025 earned a net CAGR of 14.54% against 12.71% for the equal-weighted universe, with Sharpe 0.68 against 0.65. The edge is statistically weak: the factor-regression alpha t-statistic is 0.32, and the ranked-group Spearman rho of -0.28 runs opposite to the pattern the paper reports. The simulated 2/20 fund economics are positive, with P(NPV > 0) of 76% and a median incremental fee PV of $2.0M against the equal-weighted universe fund. Robustness is rated weak, so the positive headline and economics are not yet enough to pursue, but they are enough to justify further work.

sections.paper_proposes: Jegadeesh and Titman, Profitability of Momentum Strategies: An Evaluation of Alternative Explanations, study Table 1. At the end of each month they rank NYSE/AMEX stocks on their past six-month return (month -5 to month 0), with no skip period, and sort them into ten equal-weighted decile portfolios. Each portfolio is held for six months, with overlapping monthly cohorts. The paper excludes NASDAQ stocks and stocks priced below $5. The reported past-winners minus past-losers spread is 1.11% per month (t-statistic 4.61) over 1965-1989, 1.01% per month (t 4.10) over 1990-1997, and 1.09% per month (t 5.65) over 1965-1997. The paper reads this as delayed overreaction by investors and rejects the Conrad and Kaul cross-sectional expected-return explanation.
sections.implemented_and_changed: We ranked on cum_return with months=6 and skip_months=0, formed equal-count deciles over eligible names, weighted equally, rebalanced monthly and held each cohort for 6 months. Signals use the prior month's last close and trades execute at the next month's first trading-day close, with a cost of 10 bps. Five fields were adapted. The universe is 415 names from today's S&P 500 snapshot (19 excluded for missing Yahoo data), each eligible from its index add date, so it is a survivor universe. The sample is 2015-01-01 to 2025-12-31 with a warm-up from 2012-01-01, entirely after publication. Breakpoints are equal-count sorts of eligible names, not NYSE-based. The strategy is long-only: it holds the favored group (the paper's P1, numbered group 10 in our tables) and has no short leg, although every group is computed for the monotonicity table. The paper's $5 price floor was not applied, because the snapshot's prices are split-adjusted rather than as-traded and a dollar floor would drop the wrong names. Two fields were assumed because the paper is silent: 252 days of minimum history and 15 trading days minimum in a formation month. Seven details remain unresolved and run on engine defaults: the return convention, breakpoints versus the price screen, delisting treatment, missing-data rules, share-type restrictions, weight drift within cohorts, and the return data source. Over 132 months the top decile held a mean of 36.8182 names (minimum 30, maximum 41) out of a mean of 372.288 eligible, and the overlapping cohorts held a mean of 95.6493 names per day. Cash earns zero yield, and returns use Yahoo adjusted-close conventions.
sections.backtest_found: Figures below are decimal fractions as reported in the results. Net CAGR was 0.145418 (gross 0.149617) against 0.127103 for the equal-weighted universe and 0.13453 for SPY. Net Sharpe was 0.679306 against 0.647779 for the equal-weighted universe and 0.686041 for SPY, so SPY's Sharpe is slightly higher than the strategy's. Net maximum drawdown was -0.342222, against -0.379469 for the equal-weighted universe and -0.337358 for SPY. The monthly excess return over the equal-weighted universe averaged 0.001429, with a Newey-West t of 1.09607 and a 95% interval from -0.001126 to 0.003984 that includes zero. Against SPY the mean monthly difference was 0.000976 with a Newey-West t of 0.767553. In the factor regression the annual alpha was 0.005185 with t 0.320743, and the momentum loading was 0.328854 (t 10.8912), so much of the return is explained by exposure to the momentum factor. The spanning alpha was -0.002744 with t -0.170382. By cost, alpha t was 0.548033 at 0 bps, 0.320743 at 10 bps and -0.020555 at 25 bps, where net CAGR was 0.139142. The two sub-periods look alike: net CAGR 0.145589 in 2015-2019 and 0.145275 in 2020-2025, with Sharpe 0.889037 and 0.580927 and relative-to-universe t-statistics of 0.750087 and 0.788084. The decile table does not show the paper's pattern. Group 10, the highest past return, averaged 0.012455 per month, while group 1, the lowest, averaged 0.012654, and groups 2 through 9 sat between 0.009915 and 0.010903. The favored-minus-disfavored difference was -0.000199 per month (Newey-West t -0.06847), and the rank correlation across groups was -0.284848 (p 0.425038), not in the expected direction. The engine's holds tests at 0, 10 and 25 bps and in both sub-periods returned null, and the rubric counts missing inputs as not holding, which together with the rho produces the weak robustness flag. Mean monthly turnover was 0.151131. No trade exceeded 10 percent of average daily volume at the assumed fund size.
sections.simulation_and_economics: The Monte Carlo resamples historical days in stationary blocks (mean block 126 days) over a 5-year horizon with 1000 paths. It cannot create regimes absent from the 2015-2025 sample. The fund is a long-only vehicle charged 2/20 with a 5% hard hurdle, a high-water mark and annual crystallization, discounted at 0.1. That fee schedule is an assumption, not an observed one, and incremental fees are measured against an equal-weighted universe fund charged the same schedule, never against SPY. Net of research cost (19500.1), the fraction of paths with positive NPV is 0.757, and the median incremental fee PV is $2.0M. The strategy beat the equal-weighted fund in 0.763 of paths but beat SPY in only 0.111. Median end wealth was 1.6539 for the strategy, 1.53597 for the equal-weighted fund (both net of fees) and 1.89375 for SPY (gross). The key sensitivity is that when the historical mean excess return over the equal-weighted fund is subtracted from the strategy, the fraction of paths with positive NPV falls to 0.477. The positive economics therefore depend on the edge observed in this sample persisting, and that edge has a weak t-statistic. Block-length sensitivity values were 0.723333, 0.766667 and 0.793333 for blocks of 63, 126 and 252 days.
sections.interpretation_reliability: Implementation reliability is green. The extraction used 1 run, so the field agreement of 1.0 is not a cross-run check. All 16 evidence quotes checked were valid, there were 0 consistency issues and 0 check-pass disagreements, and the paper could be implemented. Against a preliminary reference interpretation, however, agreement was only 0.357143 over 14 compared fields, with 3 critical errors (signal formula wording, holding period and favored group) and 6 minor ones. The reference is marked preliminary, and the listed differences include wording and labeling (the reference numbers the winners as P10 while the paper calls them P1), so this score should be read with caution, but we have not shown that every mismatch is only a wording difference. The 2 assumed fields, 5 adapted fields and 7 unresolved details are listed above. The engine's effort reduction is not measured. The two model calls cost 0.087404 dollars at list price.
sections.next_steps: Investigate further, with the main question being why the ranked-group pattern is flat or U-shaped in this sample instead of rising with past return. The most useful checks are a survivor-bias-free universe that includes delisted names, since the survivor universe flatters returns; a short leg or a winners-minus-losers spread that can be compared directly with the paper's 1.11% per month; a sample that includes years before publication; and an as-traded price floor to restore the paper's $5 screen. The robustness holds tests should also be rerun so that they return values instead of null. Cost should be tested above 10 bps, since alpha t turns negative at 25 bps. Treat the economics as conditional on the historical edge persisting, given the drop to 0.477 when that edge is removed.
